rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a declared emotional close that the artefact then keeps talking past, so the student's actual last impression is administrative rather than the earned payoff. That harm is present here and has grown since the last audit. Persona trace (regenerated, body_sha e45d48a3...): mid-layer close mood held at 7/10 (facilitator-premium, acceptable, unchanged); opinionated-senior close mood now 5/10, DOWN from 6/10 at the last (2026-08-15) cycle. Cause, confirmed by diff (`git diff 275bb2e HEAD -- <file>`): a repo-wide `## Optional challenges` section (4 bullets, sweep also present in getting-going.md / learn-from-the-test.md / run-the-first-experiment.md / earn-the-trust.md / plan-mode-done-right.md) was inserted between `## Key Concepts` and `## Next`. Human close still declares itself the round ('no compound prompt here... talk, compare, no prompts') and pays off its identity line ('Two sessions of the same task, read to the bone. The loop, yours.'), but is now followed by 4 closer lectures, THEN Key Concepts (recap), THEN Optional challenges (new), THEN `## Next`'s actual close -- one more section between the declaration and the real ending than the version that was last audited REVISE at 2026-08-15 (`@9c75ce2`, evidence: 'one more beat than the pre-move order carried'). The prior REVISE was never resolved; the structural tension it named is worse now, not fixed.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Narrow lens only: the Optional-challenges convention is a legitimate repo-wide pattern and its own content (skill loader, architecture eval-gate, team adoption, kit observability) is fine in isolation -- the collision is specific to M6 being the one module that declares an emotional close mid-file before the trailing sections. Worth checking whether M6's Optional challenges should sit BEFORE Human close (with the other reference/recap material), or whether Human close's 'no prompts' framing should be softened to acknowledge more follows it. Not this judge's call to resolve.
